mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying {أَكَانَ للنَّاس عجبا}: the lām in للناس is attached (mutaʿalliq) to عجب, and it is not attached to كان, because it is a verb that does not indicate an event; it indicates only time, so it is weak, and prepositions are not attached to it. Similar to it is إن كنتم للرؤيا تعبرون: the lām in للرؤيا is attached to something omitted, and تعبرون indicates the omitted element; there is disagreement about it. عجبا is the khabar (predicate) of كان, and أن أوحينا is the noun of كان, its implied form being: "Has it been a wonder to the people, Our revealing to a man among them: warn the people?".

mekki-muskil:4-4.t:
His saying {مرجعكم}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is إليه; جميعا is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf and mīm in مرجعكم.
His saying {وعد الله حَقًا}: two maṣdars (verbal nouns). What governs وعد is مرجعكم, because it has the meaning of "He has promised you a promise". Al-Farrāʾ allowed وعدُ in the nominative, making it the khabar of مرجعكم, and he allowed وعدُ and حقٌّ in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ and khabar; that is good, but no one read it so.

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying {ضِيَاء}: the second object of جعل; its meaning is "He made the sun possessed of radiance". Whoever reads it with two hamzas — the reading of Qunbul from Ibn Kathīr — has it by transposition (qalb): he fronted the hamza that is the third radical (lām al-fiʿl) into the place of the yāʾ that was changed from the wāw that is the second radical (ʿayn al-fiʿl). So the yāʾ came after the alif and the hamza before the alif, and the yāʾ was replaced by a hamza because, being radical, it occurred after an extra alif, just as they said سقاء, whose original is سقاي, because it is from سقى يسقي. It is also possible that the yāʾ, when it was moved after the alif, reverted to the wāw that is its origin, and then a hamza was substituted for it, just as they said دعاء, whose original is دعاو, because it is from دعا يدعو. So the pattern of ضئاء in the reading of Qunbul becomes فِلاع, its original being فِعال.

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying {يهْدِيهم رَبهم}: in principle هدى is made transitive both with a preposition and without a preposition, as Allah the Exalted said اهدنا الصراط, and the Exalted said فاهدوهم إلى صراط.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t: His saying {استعجالهم}: a maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "a hastening like their hastening"; then He put the adjective, which is مثل, in place of the qualified noun, which is الاستعجال, and then put the muḍāf ilayhi, which is استعجالهم, in place of the muḍāf, which is مثل. This is the view of Sībawayh. It has been said that its implied form is "in their hastening", and it has been said "like their hastening"; when the preposition was omitted it became accusative. Whoever assumes the omission of the preposition in it must allow زيدٌ الأسدَ, making الأسد accusative on the assumption "like the lion".

mekki-muskil:16-16.t:
His saying {وَلَا أدراكم}: it is related that al-Ḥasan read it with hamza [ولا أدرأتكم], but it has no basis with hamza, because one says only درأت when you repelled, and دريت in the sense of "I knew", and أدريت غيري, i.e. "I informed him".
«[Translator's note: the bracketed form is added for clarity; the text does not quote al-Ḥasan's wording.]»

mekki-muskil:21-21.t:
His saying {وَإِذا أذقنا}: إذا contains the meaning of condition but does not govern [the jussive], and it needs an apodosis (jawāb) that is not jussive, except in poetry; for in poetry the jussive may be assumed in the apodosis, and one conjoins to its meaning, putting what is conjoined to the apodosis in the jussive, as Qays ibn al-Khaṭīm said:
... إِذا قصرت أسيافنا كَانَ وَصلهَا ... خطانا إِلَى أَعْدَائِنَا فنضارب ...
(When our swords fall short, their extension is our steps towards our enemies, and so we strike.)
He put نضارب in the jussive, conjoined to the position of the apodosis of إذا, which is كان. Its apodosis according to the Basrans in this verse is His saying إذا لهم مكر, so إذا [of surprise] is the apodosis of إذا; its implied form according to them is "they plotted", and its meaning is "they mocked and denied".

mekki-muskil:23-23.t:
His saying {إِنَّمَا بَغْيكُمْ على أَنفسكُم مَتَاع الْحَيَاة الدُّنْيَا}: whoever reads متاع in the nominative makes it the khabar (predicate) of البغي; the prepositional phrase على أنفسكم is then idle (mulghā), with على attached (mutaʿalliq) to البغي, and there is no pronoun in على أنفسكم, because it is not the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject). It is also permissible to make متاع nominative by implying a mubtadaʾ, i.e. "that is an enjoyment" or "it is an enjoyment"; then على أنفسكم is the khabar of بغيكم and contains a pronoun referring back to the mubtadaʾ, with على attached to "being established" (al-istiqrār), "being fixed" or the like; its implied form [for متاع] is "your transgression is only an enjoyment of the life of this world". If you make على أنفسكم the khabar of البغي, its meaning is "your transgression only rebounds upon you", like His saying وإن أسأتم فلها. If you make متاع the khabar of البغي, its meaning is "the transgression of some of you against others is only an enjoyment of the life of this world", like the saying of the Exalted فسلموا على أنفسكم.
Ḥafṣ read from ʿĀṣim متاعَ الحياة الدنيا in the accusative. He made على أنفسكم attached to بغيكم, and البغي nominative as a mubtadaʾ with the khabar omitted, its implied form being "your transgression against yourselves for the sake of the enjoyment of the life of this world is blameworthy", or "forbidden", or "disliked", and the like; the omission is good because of the length of the speech. It is not good for على أنفسكم to be the khabar, because متاع الحياة الدنيا is included in the ṣila (relative clause / complement), so one would separate the ṣila from its relative by the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and that is not permissible; so the omission of the khabar must be assumed — unless you make متاع الحياة accusative by an implied verb, on the assumption "they enjoy an enjoyment" or "they seek an enjoyment"; then it is permissible for على أنفسكم to be the khabar.
Whoever reads متاع in the accusative makes it a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) to which البغي is extended, and implies the khabar as we mentioned; and على is attached to "being established" and the like when you make على أنفسكم the khabar, and in the genitive phrase there is a pronoun referring back to the mubtadaʾ. It is permissible to make متاع accusative as an unrestricted maṣdar (mafʿūl muṭlaq), its implied form being "they enjoy the enjoyment of the life of this world", or by implying a verb indicated by البغي, i.e. "they seek the enjoyment of the life of this world", when you make على أنفسكم the khabar.

mekki-muskil:24-24.t:
His saying {وازينت}: its original is تزينت, on the pattern تفعّلت; then the tāʾ was assimilated into the zāy, so the first became quiescent, and the connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) entered because the first letter of the verb was quiescent. The first was made quiescent in assimilation only because for every letter that you assimilate into what follows it, the first must always be made quiescent; so when the tāʾ was assimilated into the zāy the tāʾ became quiescent, and a connecting alif was needed at the start. It has many parallels in the Qurʾān.
It is related from al-Ḥasan that he read وأزينت on the pattern أفعلت, meaning "it brought forth adornment"; but according to the standards of Arabic it should have been said وأزانت, like أقالت, with the yāʾ changed into an alif. But he brought it in its original form and did not make it defective, just as استحوذ came in its original form, while the analogy would be استحاذ. It has also been read وازيانّت, like احمارّت, and it has been read وازاينت, the original being تزاينت; then the tāʾ was assimilated into the zāy on the analogy of what was mentioned before in the reading of the majority, and the connecting alif also entered it at the start on the analogy of what came before.

mekki-muskil:27-27.t:
His saying {قطعا من اللَّيْل مظلما}: مظلما is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الليل, and it is not a naʿt (adjective) of قطع, because then it would have to be said مظلمة. But in the reading of al-Kisāʾī and Ibn Kathīr, قطْعا with the ṭāʾ quiescent, it is permissible for مظلما to be a naʿt of قطع, or a ḥāl from الليل.
«[Translator's note: the text reads «باسكاء», evidently for «بإسكان» ("with quiescence").]»

mekki-muskil:28-28.t: His saying {فزيلنا بَينهم}: it is فعّلنا from زلت الشيء عن الشيء فأنا أزيله ("I removed the thing from the thing"), when you moved it aside; the doubling is for intensification. It is not permissible for it to be فعّلنا from زال يزول, because the wāw would be required in it, and one would say زوّلنا. Al-Farrāʾ reported that it was read فزايلنا, from their saying لا أزايل فلانا, i.e. "I do not part from so-and-so". As for their saying لا أزاوله, its meaning is "I do not deceive him". The meaning of زايلنا and زوّلنا is the same.

mekki-muskil:29-29.t: His saying {شَهِيدا}: accusative as a tamyīz (specification); according to Abū Isḥāq it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from Allah, exalted be His mention. بالله in His saying كفى بالله is in the position of the nominative; it is the agent of كفى, its implied form being "Allah suffices as witness", and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); its meaning is the attaching of the verb to what follows it. So Allah the Exalted has always been the One who suffices, in the sense of "He will suffice"; He never departs from that.

mekki-muskil:30-30.t: His saying {إِلَى الله مَوْلَاهُم الْحق}: مولى is a badal (substitute) from الله, or a naʿt (adjective); and الحق is also a naʿt of it. Making it accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) is permissible, but it was not read so.

mekki-muskil:33-33.t: His saying {أَنهم لَا يُؤمنُونَ}: أنّ is in the position of the accusative, its implied form being "in that they…" or "because they…"; when the preposition was omitted the verb became transitive and made the position accusative. The open أنّ, whether doubled or lightened, is always a particle on its own, and a noun together with what follows it, because it and what follows it are a maṣdar (verbal noun), assigned the case endings according to the governing word before it. It is also permissible that it be in the position of the genitive by the omitted preposition; that is the view of al-Khalīl: because its omission is frequent with أنّ specifically, it governs while omitted as it governs when present in the wording. It has also been said that this verse [i.e. this clause] is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from كلمات, and this is a good view; it is the substitution of a thing for a thing which is itself.

mekki-muskil:35-35.t:
His saying {أَفَمَن يهدي إِلَى الْحق أَحَق أَن يتبع}: من is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أحق is the khabar (predicate). In the speech there is an omission, its implied form being "more deserving than one who does not guide". أن is in the position of the accusative on the assumption of the omission of the preposition. If you wish, you make it in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from من — it is badal al-ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) — with أحق the khabar. And if you wish, you make أن a second mubtadaʾ with أحق its khabar fronted before it, and the clause the khabar of من.
His saying {فَمَا لكم}: ما is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; it is interrogative, and its meaning is rebuke and alerting. لكم is the khabar, and the speech is complete at لكم. The meaning is "What is there for you in the worship of idols?".

mekki-muskil:37-37.t: His saying {وَلَكِن تَصْدِيق الَّذِي بَين يَدَيْهِ}: تصديق is the khabar (predicate) of an implied كان, its implied form being "but it was a confirmation", so كان contains its noun. This is the view of al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī. According to them the nominative is also permissible, on the assumption "but it is a confirmation".

mekki-muskil:44-44.t:
His saying {وَلَكِن النَّاس}: the preference according to a group of grammarians is that when لكن comes with the wāw it be doubled (لكنّ), and when there is no wāw before it, it be lightened (لكنْ). Al-Farrāʾ said: because when it is without a wāw it resembles بل, so it was lightened to be like it in correction (istidrāk); and when the wāw comes before it, it differs from بل, so it was doubled. The Kufans allowed introducing the lām into its khabar (predicate), as with إنّ, and they cited:
... ولكنني من حبها لكميد ...
(But I, from love of her, am indeed grief-stricken.)
The Basrans rejected it, because its meaning differs from the meaning of إنّ. Whoever doubles it makes it govern what follows it and puts it in the accusative by it, because it is one of the sisters of إنّ; and whoever lightens it puts what follows it in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with what follows that as its khabar.
«[Translator's note: the text reads «في خبرها كان», evidently for «كأنّ» or «كإنّ»; it is translated as "as with إنّ".]»

mekki-muskil:45-45.t: His saying {وَيَوْم يحشرهم كَأَن لم يَلْبَثُوا}: the kāf of كأن and what follows it are in the position of the accusative as an adjective of اليوم. In the speech there is the omission of a pronoun referring back to the qualified noun, its implied form being "as though they had not tarried before it"; then قبل was omitted, so the hāʾ became attached to يلبثوا, and it was then omitted because of the length of the noun, just as it is omitted from relative clauses. It is also permissible that the kāf of كأن be in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "and on the day He gathers them, a gathering as though they had not tarried before it except an hour". It is also permissible that the kāf be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and mīm in يحشرهم, with the pronoun in يلبثوا referring back to the owner of the ḥāl, and no omission in the speech; its implied form is "and on the day He gathers them, their states resembling the states of those who tarried only an hour". What makes يوم accusative is an implied اذكر ("remember"), and it is also permissible that what makes it accusative be يتعارفون.

mekki-muskil:50-50.t: His saying {مَاذَا يستعجل مِنْهُ المجرمون}: ما is interrogative, nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the meaning of the interrogative here is threat. ذا is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, in the sense of الذي, and the hāʾ in منه refers back to the punishment. If you wish, you make ما and ذا a single noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar in the clause after it, and the hāʾ in منه also referring back to the punishment. If you make the hāʾ in منه refer back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and ما and ذا a single noun, then ما is in the position of the accusative by يستعجل, and the meaning is "What thing do the criminals seek to hasten from Allah?".

mekki-muskil:53-53.t: His saying {أَحَق هُوَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the second object of يستنبئونك, if you make it mean "they ask you to tell". If you make it mean "they ask you to inform [with knowledge]", then أحق هو is a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of its two [remaining] objects, because أنبأ, when it means أعلم ("inform"), is transitive to three objects; it may be content with one, but it may not be content with two without the third. When أنبأ means أخبر ("tell"), it is transitive to two objects, and it may not be content with one without the second. نبّأ and أنبأ are equal in transitivity.

mekki-muskil:61-61.t:
His saying {وَمَا تتلو مِنْهُ من قُرْآن}: the hāʾ, according to al-Farrāʾ, refers back to الشأن ("the affair"), on the assumption of the omission of a muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct), its implied form being "and you do not recite on account of the affair", i.e. an affair arises for you and you recite the Qurʾān on account of it.
His saying {وَلَا أَصْغَر من ذَلِك وَلَا أكبر}: أصغر and أكبر, in the reading of whoever reads them with fatḥa, are in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the wording of مثقال ذرة. Ḥamza read both in the nominative, conjoining them to the position of مثقال, because it is in the position of the nominative by يعزب.

mekki-muskil:63-63.t: His saying {الَّذين آمنُوا وَكَانُوا يَتَّقُونَ}: الذين is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from the noun of إنّ, which is أولياء, or on [the implied verb] أعني ("I mean"). The nominative is also permissible: as a badal from the position, as a naʿt (adjective) on the position, by implying a mubtadaʾ (subject), or as a mubtadaʾ — with لهم البشرى, a mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate), in the position of the khabar of الذين.

mekki-muskil:66-66.t: His saying {وَمَا يتبع الَّذين يدعونَ من دون الله شُرَكَاء}: شركاء is accusative by يدعون, and the object of يتبع is supplied by إن يتبعون إلا الظن, because it is the same thing. شركاء is not made accusative by يتبع, because you would be negating that of them, whereas Allah has reported it of them. If you made ما interrogative with the sense of disapproval and rebuke, it would be a noun in the position of the accusative by يتبع; on the first view ما is a negating particle.

mekki-muskil:71-71.t:
His saying {فَأَجْمعُوا أَمركُم وشركاءكم}: all the readers read it with hamza and kasra on the mīm, from their saying أجمعت على أمر كذا وكذا when you resolved upon it; أجمعت الأمر without a preposition is also good, as Allah, exalted be His mention, said إذ أجمعوا أمرهم. The accusative of الشركاء is then by conjunction according to the meaning; that is the view of al-Mubarrad. Al-Zajjāj said: it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment). It has been said that الشركاء is conjoined to الأمر, because its implied form is "so gather those of authority among you". It has been said that the interpretation of الأمر here is their scheme, so الشركاء is conjoined to الأمر without omission. It has been said that الشركاء is accusative by an omitted governing word, its implied form being "and gather (اجمعوا) your partners", so أجمع indicated جمع; because you say جمعت الشركاء والقوم ("I gathered the partners and the people"), but you do not say أجمعت الشركاء — one says أجمعت only of a matter specifically. For that reason conjoining الشركاء to الأمر was not good on the assumption given earlier. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: its implied form is "and call your partners", and so it is in the ḥarf (reading) of Ubayy: وادعوا شركاءكم.
Al-Aṣmaʿī related from Nāfiʿ فاجمعوا with the connecting alif and fatḥa on the mīm; on this reading conjoining الشركاء to الأمر is good, and it is good for the wāw to mean "with". Al-Ḥasan read الشركاء in the nominative, conjoined to the implied nominative pronoun in فاجمعوا, and Yaʿqūb al-Ḥaḍramī read so; what made that good is the separation that occurred between the conjoined word and the pronoun, as though it stood in place of the tawkīd (emphasis), namely أمركم.

mekki-muskil:74-74.t: His saying {بِمَا كذبُوا بِهِ}: the pronoun in كذبوا refers back to the people of Noah, i.e. "the people of the messengers who were sent after Noah were not going to believe in what the people of Noah had denied"; rather, they denied like the denial of the people of Noah.

mekki-muskil:81-81.t:
His saying {مَا جئْتُمْ بِهِ السحر}: ما is a mubtadaʾ (subject) in the sense of الذي, جئتم به is its ṣila (relative clause), and السحر is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. This is supported by the fact that in the ḥarf (reading) of Ubayy it is ما جئتم به سحر. Everything we have mentioned in this book of ours and elsewhere from the reading of Ubayy and others that differs from the script of the Muṣḥaf is not to be recited, because it differs from the Muṣḥaf; we mention it only as evidence, not so that it be recited — so know that.
It is permissible for ما to be nominative as a mubtadaʾ, being interrogative, with جئتم به the khabar and السحر the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "it is sorcery". It is permissible for ما to be in the position of the accusative by an implied verb after it, its implied form being "what thing have you brought?", with السحر the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. It is not permissible for ما in the sense of الذي to be in the position of the accusative, because what follows it is its ṣila, and the ṣila does not govern the relative noun, nor does it serve as the explanation of the governing word of the relative noun.
Abū ʿAmr read آلسحر with prolongation. On this reading ما is interrogative, جئتم به is the khabar, and السحر is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "is it sorcery?". On this reading ما may not be in the sense of الذي, since it would have no khabar. It is permissible for ما to be in the position of the accusative as stated before. And it is permissible to make السحر nominative as a badal (substitute) from ما, with its khabar being the khabar of what is substituted for; therefore the interrogative entered it, since it is a substitute for an interrogative, so that the substitute and what is substituted for are equal in the form of interrogation — just as you say كم مالك أعشرون أم ثلاثون ("How much is your wealth — twenty or thirty?"), making عشرون a badal from كم and putting the interrogative alif on عشرين, because what is substituted for, namely كم, is interrogative. The meaning of the interrogative in this verse is confirmation and rebuke, and it is not a request for information, because Moses, upon him be peace, knew that it was sorcery; he only rebuked them for what they did and did not ask them about something he did not know. It also contains the meaning of belittling what they brought.
Al-Farrāʾ allowed السحرَ in the accusative: he made ما conditional and السحر accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), with the fāʾ implied with إن الله سيبطله, and the alif and lām in السحر made redundant. All of that is far-fetched. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān allowed dropping the fāʾ from the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) in ordinary speech, and cited as proof of its permissibility the saying of the Exalted وما أصابكم من مصيبة بما كسبت أيديكم; no one else allowed it except by poetic necessity.

mekki-muskil:83-83.t:
His saying {من فِرْعَوْن وملئهم}: the pronoun in ملئهم was made plural only because it is a statement about a tyrant, and a tyrant is spoken of with the plural form. It has been said: since Pharaoh was mentioned with the implication that others were with him, the pronoun referred back to him and to those with him. It has been said that the pronoun refers back to the people (آل) of Pharaoh, and there is an omission in the speech, the implied form being "in fear of the people of Pharaoh and their chiefs", with the pronoun referring back to الآل. Al-Akhfash said: the pronoun refers back to the offspring (الذرية) mentioned earlier. It has been said that the pronoun refers back to the people (القوم) mentioned earlier.
His saying {أَن يفتنهم}: أن is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from فرعون; it is badal al-ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion).

mekki-muskil:88-88.t: His saying {فَلَا يُؤمنُوا}: conjoined to ليضلوا, in the position of the accusative according to al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjāj. Al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ said: it is accusative as the answer to the supplication. Al-Kisāʾī and Abū ʿUbayda said: it is in the position of the jussive, because it is a supplication against them.

mekki-muskil:92-92.t:
His saying {ننجيك ببدنك}: it has been said that it is from النجاء, i.e. "We will rescue you from the sea dead, so that the Children of Israel may see you"; and it has been said that its meaning is "We will cast you onto a raised place (نجوة) of the land".
His saying {ببدنك}, i.e. "with your coat of mail by which you are recognised, so that the Children of Israel may see you"; it has also been said that the meaning of ببدنك is "with your body, with no soul in you, so that the Children of Israel may see you".
«[Translator's note: the text reads «النحاء», evidently for «النجاء».]»

mekki-muskil:98-98.t:
His saying {إِلَّا قوم يُونُس}: قوم is accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). It is also permissible that it be a connected exception, on the assumption that the omission of a muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct) is implied in the speech, its implied form being "Why was there not the people of a town that believed…?". The nominative is also permissible, by making إلا in the sense of غير, an adjective of the omitted "people" in meaning; then what comes after إلا is declined as غير would be declined if it appeared in the place of إلا. Al-Farrāʾ allowed the nominative as a badal (substitute), as [the poet] said:
... وبلدة لَيْسَ بهَا أنيس ... إِلَّا اليعافير وَإِلَّا العيس ...
(And many a land with no companion in it except young gazelles and white camels.)
He substituted [them] for أنيس, though the second is not of the same kind. This is the dialect of Banū Tamīm: they substitute even if the second is not of the same kind as the first, whereas the people of the Ḥijāz use the accusative when the two differ, even if the speech is negative. They cited the verse of al-Nābigha:
.. إِلَّا أواري لايا مَا أبينها ...
(Except tethering-posts which I could barely make out.)
with the nominative and the accusative.
His saying {يُونُس}: it is a foreign (ʿajamī) proper name, and for that reason it is a diptote; similar to it is يوسف. It is related from al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim that they read يونِس and يوسِف with kasra on the nūn and the sīn, making them imperfect verbs from أنس and أسف used as names, so they are diptotes because of definiteness and the pattern specific to verbs. Abū Ḥātim said: they ought to be pronounced with hamza, though dropping the hamza is permissible and good, even if its origin is with hamza. Abū Zayd reported fatḥa on the nūn and the sīn in both, as passive imperfect verbs, also used as names.
